The probe explicitly attempts writes at PROBE_READONLY/forbidden-write, /dev/forbidden-write and /dev/shm/forbidden-write. Every write must raise EROFS or ENOENT; a successful write rejects the probe. /dev/null write and RAM witness are positives.
Output and restore are separately capped tmpfs; TMPDIR/cache/object outputs are declared writable. Archive/full restore and exact intentional-kill evidence are checked.

interpretation.conclusion: No inspected original user/master/binding gate states that every diagnostic must forever deny writes to the pathname /dev/shm irrespective of what private object is mounted there. The exact literal denial is a binding predicate for the currently qualified RAMv2/v3 mechanism, not a general prohibition on declared private RAM output.
interpretation.permissible_design_lane: A NEW immutable diagnostic profile may be considered under routine isolated-engineering authority if its only new writable mapping is an alias of an existing capped private output directory, host data/principals remain protected, all resource/evidence gates remain, and independently fixed successor controls prove that boundary. This is a new qualification subject, not a passing re-run of the old predicate.
interpretation.original_fixture_rule: Preserve old v2/v3 sources, fixtures, expected outcomes, failures and exact approval under their original topology. Do not edit their /dev/shm assertion, relabel a writable result as the old forbidden-write pass, or claim AST-identical/unchanged-mechanism inheritance.
interpretation.approval_boundary: A user waiver is not established as necessary solely from a demonstrably private capped alias. If the actual proposal drops a binding negative control without equivalent boundary evidence, allows host writes, skips accepted cases, raises a cap or weakens retention/rejection, it is a deviation: explicit user approval is required by the user's universal instructions. Reviewer concurrence cannot grant that waiver.
interpretation.current_disposition: Source preparation and independent review are eligible; no current approval transfers to a launch. No claim that a concrete successor already preserves all guarantees is made.

technical_assessment.alias_budget: Binding a subdirectory of the already capped output tmpfs can reuse its existing aggregate byte/inode ceiling instead of adding another filesystem allowance. Verify the actual filesystem identity and limits; a bind alone supplies no size cap.
technical_assessment.isolation: Add --unshare-ipc as an independently checked namespace boundary. Do not treat it as a substitute for a private /dev/shm mount, a filesystem pathname-socket boundary or a resource cap.
technical_assessment.caveat: New IPC namespaces do not establish a whole-system noninterference proof. Namespace-owned resources outside the bound filesystem still require the existing cgroup boundary and a precise claim; do not claim every possible IPC allocation is capped by the tmpfs byte limit.
technical_assessment.retention: Keep unsupported-entry rejection and full archive/restore requirements. If a socket survives tool termination, report incomplete retention; do not skip, unlink for cosmetic success, archive it as a regular file or infer proof credit.
